units.source_text: 邸内器具什物，都是上代用惯了的，古色古香，精致华丽。

en.t: The furnishings and utensils in the residence had all been used since earlier generations, antique in style, refined, and splendid.

units.source_text: 有几个一知半解的暴发户，垂涎这些器物，

en.t: A few newly rich people with only half-baked knowledge coveted these objects,

units.source_text: 特地探听出某物为某名匠所作，某物为某专家所造，托人介绍，希图购取。

en.t: and went out of their way to find out that one item had been made by a certain master craftsman and another by a certain specialist, then asked others to introduce them, hoping to buy the pieces.

units.source_text: 自然是看不起这贫困人家，故敢肆意侮辱。

en.t: Naturally, they looked down on this impoverished household, and so dared to insult it as they pleased.

units.source_text: 那些侍女有时就说：“无可奈何了！

en.t: The serving women would sometimes say, "There is nothing we can do!

units.source_text: 出卖器物，也是世间常有之事。”

en.t: Selling household objects is also something that often happens in the world."

units.source_text: 想胡乱成就交易，以救燃眉之急。

en.t: They wanted to settle a transaction somehow, in order to meet their most urgent need.

units.source_text: 末摘花说：“这些器具是老大人留给我使用的，

en.t: Suetsumuhana said, "These implements were left by my late father for me to use,

units.source_text: 岂可作为下等人家的饰物？

en.t: so how could they become ornaments in some inferior household?

units.source_text: 违背先人本意，是罪过的！”

en.t: To go against my ancestor's intention would be a sin!"
She absolutely would not let them sell the things.
